title: SKU Flexification & Enterprise Security Questionnaire Alignment for Dedicated GPUs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a controlled experiment to introduce a compact SKU taxonomy for Dedicated GPU capacity that supports fine-grained autoscale, a transparent burst-credit mechanism, and a standard set of answers for enterprise security questionnaires (SQs). Goal: reduce sales friction, improve forecastability for customers, and ensure security/legal readiness for enterprise contracts. Deliverables: SKU definitions, pricing bands, burst credit rules, autoscale governance, updated sales-facing docs, and a completed SQ template mapped to technical controls.
acceptance_criteria: SKU taxonomy documented and approved by Product and Sales
Pricing bands validated with 3 pilot customers and no negative margin below threshold
Autoscale behavior simulated against historical workloads with telemetry confirming latency SLAs maintained
Burst-credit policy defined (earn/use/recovery) and implemented in billing mock for evaluation
Security questionnaire (top 20 enterprise questions) drafted with engineering-provided evidence links and legal sign-off
Sales enablement materials (one-pager + pricing calculator) published to Drive and linked in CRM
steps: 1) Audit existing dedicated SKUs, usage patterns and recent enterprise RFPs
2) Workshop SKU shapes with Sales, Finance, and Infra (target: 3 core SKUs + 2 flex addons)
3) Prototype burst-credit accounting in billing simulator (Eng)
4) Run 2-week autoscale simulation using historical request traces (Eng/Infra)
5) Draft SQ responses and evidence bundle; review with Security and Legal
6) Pilot with 3 mid-market customers and iterate pricing/terms
7) Finalize sales docs, contract language, and internal enablement
decisions: Adopt 3-tier SKU base (Compact/Standard/Compute-Heavy) + burst-credit add-on rather than per-GPU micro-SKUs to limit sales complexity
Burst credits will be soft-limited with a recovery window (14 days) to avoid long-term overcommit exposure
Autoscale granularity set to 5-minute decision intervals with a hard cap equal to committed capacity + burst allowance
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs. precision: fewer SKUs reduces confusion but may under-index for very spiky workloads
Predictability vs. upside: soft burst credits improve availability but risk marginally higher peak costs for provider
Sales velocity vs. custom legal terms: standardized SQ answers speed deals but may require exceptions for large customers
notes: Finance requires a modeled 10% gross margin floor across pilot pricing bands
Legal flagged audit-log evidence gaps for on-prem Private deployments; Security to scope remediation
Engineering suggested pre-warming strategy for predictable latency during burst windows (warm pools + fast spin-up)
